This code was used in the analysis of Gamache et al. (2026) (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00125-026-06722-5). For the purpose of my analysis we did not use the sex-stratified results. 

# _______________________________

# Package
```{r}
library(nlme)
library(lme4)
library(geepack)
library("tidyverse")
library(reshape2)
library(car)
library(texreg)
library(performance)
```

# _______________________________

# Functions

## Pre-process

This function prepares the longitudinal data for GEE analyses by converting the visit indicator into a continuous time variable based on the mean age at each visit, removing observations with missing outcome values, and centering time at the earliest visit.

```{r}
prepareGEEData = function(mydata_long, phenotype, bySex =TRUE) {
    allData=c()
    for (i in unique(mydata_long$time)) { # For each visit
      allData=rbind(allData,mydata_long[mydata_long$time==i,])
      allData[allData$time == i, 'time'] = round(mean(allData[allData$time == i, 'age_yrs'], na.rm = TRUE), digits = 2)
    }
    
    # Remove line with NA
    mydata_long = allData[!is.na(allData[, phenotype]), ]
    
    # Put the time at 0
    mydata_long$time = mydata_long$time - min(mydata_long$time) # Comment line when doing plots 
    
    # Finished the scaling
    return(mydata_long)
}

```

## Pre-process 

This is another pre-process function for the analyses which contain environmental variables 

```{r}
scaleTheVariableAndRemoveOutlier = function(mydata_long, phenotype, bySex =TRUE) {
    allData=c() # Will contain all the processed data
    for (i in unique(mydata_long$time)) { # By visit
        if (bySex == TRUE) {
            # Male
            dataM=mydata_long[mydata_long$time == i & mydata_long$sex==1,] # Extract male and this visit
            dataM=dataM[!is.na(dataM[,phenotype]),] # Remove NA
            meana = mean(dataM[, phenotype], na.rm = TRUE) # Get mean
            sd = sd(dataM[, phenotype], na.rm = TRUE) # Get SD
            
            dataM=dataM[dataM[,phenotype]>= (meana - 5 * sd) & dataM[,phenotype]<= (meana + 5 * sd),]
            dataM[,phenotype]=scale(dataM[,phenotype])
            
            allData=rbind(allData,dataM)
           
  
            # Female
            dataF=mydata_long[mydata_long$time == i & mydata_long$sex==2,]
            dataF=dataF[!is.na(dataF[,phenotype]),]
            meana = mean(dataF[, phenotype], na.rm = TRUE)
            sd = sd(dataF[, phenotype], na.rm = TRUE)
            
            dataF=dataF[dataF[,phenotype]>= (meana - 5 * sd) & dataF[,phenotype]<= (meana + 5 * sd),]
            
            dataF[,phenotype]=scale(dataF[,phenotype])
            
            allData=rbind(allData,dataF)
            
        } else{
            dataT=mydata_long[mydata_long$time == i,]
            meana = mean(dataT[, phenotype], na.rm = TRUE)
            sd = sd(dataT[, phenotype], na.rm = TRUE)
            
            dataT=dataT[dataT[,phenotype]>= (meana - 5 * sd) & dataT[,phenotype]<= (meana + 5 * sd),]
            
            dataT[,phenotype]=scale(dataT[,phenotype])
            
            allData=rbind(allData,dataT)
        }
        
       allData[allData$time == i, 'time'] = round(mean(allData[allData$time == i, 'age_yrs'], na.rm = TRUE),digits=2)
        
        
    }
    
    mydata_long = allData[!is.na(allData[,phenotype]), ]
    mydata_long$time = mydata_long$time - min(mydata_long$time) 
    
    return(mydata_long)
}

```

## Check 1: Mean outcome trajectory over time
Calculate the mean outcome at each visit to assess the overall trajectory of the phenotype over time. This generates a plot, you need to verify if the mean across time seems constant. 

```{r}
check1_MeanAcrossTime <- function(mydata_long, phenotype) {
  moy <- (aggregate(Phenotype ~ time, data = mydata_long, mean, na.rm = T))
  colnames(moy)[2] = 'Phenotype' # outcome of interest
  plot(
    moy$time,
    moy[, 'Phenotype'],
    pch = 17,
    xlab = 'Visit',
    ylab = paste0(phenotype, ' z-score')
  )
  lines(moy$time, moy[, 'Phenotype'], lty = 2)
  title(phenotype)
}

```

## Check 2: Selection of the time trajectory
Fit candidate linear models to determine whether the association between the phenotype and VAR changes linearly or non-linearly over time (time, time squared or interaction with time).

```{r}
check2_BestLinearModel <- function(mydata_long, allResult_S, var = 'NotSex', adjust_maternal_age = TRUE) {
  
  # Will keep in memory if the model was evaluated
  smod1 = FALSE
  smod2 = FALSE
  smod3 = FALSE
  smod4 = FALSE
  
  mod1 = NULL
  mod2 = NULL
  mod3 = NULL
  mod4 = NULL
  
  # Define covariates
  covariates <- c()
  
  # Add sex when analysis is not sex-stratified and VAR is not sex
  if (whichSex == 0 && var != 'sex') {
    covariates <- c(covariates, "sex")
  }
  
  # Add maternal age when required (when the analysis is not child specific)
  if (adjust_maternal_age) {
    covariates <- c(covariates, "AgeDelivery_Mom")
  }
  
  # Construct the covariate portion of the model
  covariates <- if (length(covariates) > 0) {
    paste(covariates, collapse = " + ")
  } else { "" }
  
  # MODEL 1: Linear association with time
  formula1 <- as.formula(
      paste("Phenotype ~ VAR + time",
            ifelse(covariates != "", paste("+", covariates), ""))
    )  
  mod1 <- glm(formula1, data = mydata_long, family=binomial)
  smod1 = TRUE # This model was estimated

  # MODEL 2: Add a quadratic time term 
  # I(time^2) creates the squared time term directly within the model.
  formula2 <- as.formula(
    paste("Phenotype ~ VAR + time + I(time^2)",
          ifelse(covariates != "", paste("+", covariates), ""))
  )
  mod2 <- glm(formula2, data = mydata_long, family=binomial)
  smod2 = TRUE # This model was estimated
  
  # MODEL 3: Allow the effect of VAR to vary linearly over time
  # The VAR * time interaction tests whether the association between VAR and the phenotype changes across visits.
  formula3 <- as.formula(
    paste("Phenotype ~ time * VAR + I(time^2)",
          ifelse(covariates != "", paste("+", covariates), ""))
  )
  mod3 <- glm(formula3, data = mydata_long, family=binomial)
  
  # Determine whether the VAR × time interaction is statistically significant. Only if there is evidence that the effect of VAR changes over time do we proceed to the more complex Model 4.
  
  if (summary(mod3)$coefficient['time:VAR', 4] < 0.05) { # You only consider this if the term is significant.
    smod3 = TRUE

    # MODEL 4: Allow the effect of VAR to vary non-linearly over time
    # Create a squared-time variable for use in Model 4.
    mydata_long$timesq <- mydata_long$time^2
    
    formula4 <- as.formula(
    paste("Phenotype ~ time * VAR + timesq * VAR",
          ifelse(covariates != "", paste("+", covariates), ""))
    )
    mod4 <- glm(formula4, data = mydata_long, family=binomial)
    
    # Determine whether the VAR × time^2 interaction is statistically significant.
    # If significant, Model 4 is retained as a candidate for BIC-based model selection. Otherwise, Model 4 is excluded.
    if (summary(mod4)$coefficient['VAR:timesq', 4] < 0.05) { 
      smod4 = TRUE
      bic = BIC(mod1, mod2, mod3, mod4) 
      best_model_linear = rownames(bic[which.min(bic$BIC), ]) 
    } else{
      bic = BIC(mod1, mod2, mod3)
      best_model_linear = rownames(bic[which.min(bic$BIC), ]) 
    }
  } else{
    bic = BIC(mod1, mod2)
    best_model_linear = rownames(bic[which.min(bic$BIC), ]) 
  }
  
  # Store the BIC value for each model. Models that were not evaluated will have NA because they are absent
  # from the BIC table.
  
  bmod1 = bic['mod1', 'BIC']
  bmod2 = bic['mod2', 'BIC']
  bmod3 = bic['mod3', 'BIC']
  bmod4 = bic['mod4', 'BIC']
  
  allResult_S$bic_mod1 = bmod1
  allResult_S$bic_mod2 = bmod2
  allResult_S$bic_mod3 = bmod3
  allResult_S$bic_mod4 = bmod4
  
  # Conserve all informations obtain from this function in the table, this will be used in other function
  allResult_S$best_linear_model = best_model_linear
  
  # Compile all informations and return them
  out = list(
    allResult_S = allResult_S,
    smod1 = smod1,
    smod2 = smod2,
    smod3 = smod3,
    smod4 = smod4,
    mod1 = mod1,
    mod2 = mod2,
    mod3 = mod3,
    mod4 = mod4
  )
  return(out)
}

```


## Check 3: Predictions from candidate models
Generate predicted phenotype values from each candidate model evaluated in Check 2 and compare them with the observed mean phenotype trajectory across visits. Predictions are generated only for models that were successfully fitted. The resulting plot shows how well each model captures the observed phenotype trajectory over time.

```{r}
check3_Prediction <- function(mydata_long, smod1, smod2, smod3, smod4, mod1, mod2, mod3, mod4, var='NotSex') {
  
  # If not sex-stratified or if the factor is the not sex, we will add sex to the models
  if (whichSex != 0 || var == 'sex') {
    datapred = mydata_long %>% drop_na(c("VAR", "Phenotype", "time"))
  } else{
    datapred = mydata_long %>% drop_na(c("VAR", "Phenotype", "time", "sex"))
  }
  
  
 # smod1–smod4 indicate whether the corresponding model was fitted.
  if (smod1)
    datapred$p1 <- predict(mod1, newdata = datapred)
  if (smod2)
    datapred$p2 <- predict(mod2, newdata = datapred)
  if (smod3)
    datapred$p3 <- predict(mod3, newdata = datapred)
  if (smod4)
    datapred$p4 <- predict(mod4, newdata = datapred)
  
  # Calculate the observed mean phenotype at each visit
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  
  moy <- aggregate(Phenotype ~ VAR + time, data = mydata_long, mean, na.rm = T)
  colnames(moy)[3] = 'Phenotype'
  
   # Plot the observed mean phenotype trajectory.
  plot(
    moy$time,
    moy$Phenotype,
    pch = 4,
    xlab = 'Visit',
    ylab = paste0(phenotype, ' z-score')
  )
  
  lines(moy$time, moy$Phenotype, lty = 3, col = 1)
  
  last = 1
  # mod1
  if (smod1) {
    points(datapred$time, datapred$p1, col = 2)
    lines(datapred$time, datapred$p1, lty = 3, col = 2)
    last = 2
  }
  
  # mod2
  if (smod2) {
    points(datapred$time, datapred$p2, col = 3)
    lines(datapred$time, datapred$p2, lty = 3, col = 3)
    last = 3
  }
  
  # mod3
  if (smod3) {
    points(datapred$time, datapred$p3, col = 4)
    lines(datapred$time, datapred$p3, lty = 3, col = 4)
    last = 4
  }
  
  # mod4
  if (smod4) {
    points(datapred$time, datapred$p4, col = 5)
    lines(datapred$time, datapred$p4, lty = 3, col = 5)
    last = 5
  }
  
  legend(
    'bottomright',
    col = 1:last,
    lty = 1,
    legend = c("Mean", "Linear", "Quadratic", "VAR*Time", "VAR*Time2")[1:last]
  )
  return(datapred)
}
```

## GEE - Extract results
This function fits two GEE models using the model specifications selected in the previous steps: one model without the exposure-by-time interaction and one model including the interaction.

```{r}

extract_results <-function(allResult,allResult_S,mydata_long, formula, formula2, best_model_linear){

  
  # ==============================
  # 1. Get all variables needed
  formula_vars <- unique(c(all.vars(as.formula(formula)), 
                           all.vars(as.formula(formula2)), "IID"))

  # 2. Remove NAs FIRST
  mydata_clean <- na.omit(mydata_long[, formula_vars])
  
  # 3. THEN rank and order
  mydata_clean$IID = dplyr::min_rank(mydata_clean$IID)
  mydata_clean = mydata_clean[order(mydata_clean$IID), ]
  
  # ==============================
  
  m1_cont <- geeglm(
    as.formula(formula),
    data = mydata_clean, # before it was mydata_long
    id = IID,
    family = binomial,
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  
  m1_int <- geeglm(
    as.formula(formula2),
    data = mydata_clean,
    id = IID,
    family = binomial,
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  
  #summarize an lme object (gets beta hat, se, t-value, p-value for fixed effects)
  outputm1 <- (texreg::extract(m1_cont))
  tabl = data.frame(Name=attr(outputm1,'coef.names'),Value=attr(outputm1,'coef'),Std.Error=attr(outputm1,'se'),p.value=attr(outputm1,'pvalues'))
  rownames(tabl)=tabl$Name
  tabl
  
  # summarize a lme object (gets beta hat, se, t-value, p-value for fixed effects)
  outputm1 <- (texreg::extract(m1_int))
  tabl_int = data.frame(Name=attr(outputm1,'coef.names'),Value=attr(outputm1,'coef'),Std.Error=attr(outputm1,'se'),p.value=attr(outputm1,'pvalues'))
  rownames(tabl_int)=tabl_int$Name
  tabl_int
  
  # Extract results from the table, depending on the best fitting models. 
  if (best_model_linear %in% c('mod1', 'mod2')) {
    allResult_S$formula_cont = formula # Will keep the formula of the model WITHOUT interaction
    
    # Get the VAR association results WITHOUT interaction
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_b = tabl['VAR', 'Value'] 
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_se = tabl['VAR', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_p = tabl['VAR', 'p.value']
    
    ##########
    # Get results from interaction
    allResult_S$formula_int = formula2
    
    # Get the VAR association results WITHOUT interaction, from the models WITH time-interaction
    allResult_S$VAR_int_b = tabl_int['VAR', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VAR_int_se = tabl_int['VAR', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VAR_int_p = tabl_int['VAR', 'p.value']
    
    # Get the VAR*time association from the models WITH time-interaction
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_b = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_se = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_p = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'p.value']
    
    # Not applicable for this models, but need the column
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_b = NA
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_se = NA
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_p = NA
    
  } else if (best_model_linear %in% c('mod3')) { # Never tested, but really similar to above, but we switch formula and formula2 since the interaction is present in formula, but not formula2
    allResult_S$formula_cont = formula
    
    # Get VAR results without time-interaction
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_b = tabl['VAR', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_se = tabl['VAR', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_p = tabl['VAR', 'p.value']
    
    #################
    # Formula with VAR*time interaction
    allResult_S$formula_int = formula2
    
    # Get VAR results WITHOUT interaction from model WITH time interaction
    allResult_S$VAR_int_b = tabl_int['VAR', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VAR_int_se = tabl_int['VAR', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VAR_int_p = tabl_int['VAR', 'p.value']
    
    # Extract VAR*time results
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_b = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_se = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_p = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'p.value']
    
    # Not applicable for this models
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_b = NA
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_se = NA
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_p = NA
    
  } else if (best_model_linear %in% c('mod4')) { # The more complex model
    
    # Will extract the VAR result from the simplest formula of the two models
    allResult_S$formula_cont = formula2
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_b = tabl['VAR', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_se = tabl['VAR', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VAR_cont_p = tabl['VAR', 'p.value']
    
    #############
    # Complex models
    allResult_S$formula_int = formula
    
    # VAR WITHOUT interaction from the model WITH interaction
    allResult_S$VAR_int_b = tabl_int['VAR', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VAR_int_se = tabl_int['VAR', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VAR_int_p = tabl_int['VAR', 'p.value']
    
    # VAR*time interaction form the model WITH interaction
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_b = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_se = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VARtime_int_p = tabl_int['VAR:time', 'p.value']
    
    # VAR*time2 interaction
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_b = tabl_int['VAR:timesq', 'Value']
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_se = tabl_int['VAR:timesq', 'Std.Error']
    allResult_S$VARtime2_int_p = tabl_int['VAR:timesq', 'p.value']
  }
  
  # combine
  allResult = rbind(allResult, allResult_S)
  
  return(allResult)
}
```

## Helper function getColumn()
This function extracts the selected environmental variable from the original dataset, formats it according to the available measurement visits, and merges it with the longitudinal outcome dataset.

```{r}
getColumn <- function(mydata_long, var, age) {
  
  # Identify all columns corresponding to the environmental variable.
  allEnv = colnames(df)[grep(var, colnames(df))] 
  
  # Select variables for child analyses.
  if (age == 'Child') {
    
    if (!grepl('Mom', var) & sum(grepl('Mom', allEnv) != 0)) {
      allEnv = allEnv[-grep('Mom', allEnv)]
    }
    
    # This will be specific to your dataset.
    # Remove variables that do not correspond to the required measurement visits or should otherwise be excluded.
    allEnv = allEnv[!(
      allEnv %in% c(
        'PredictedEnergyIntakeKCAL_3yrs',
        'MPVAsedentary_F13',
        'MPVAmvpa_F13',
        'MVPAcpm_F13',
        'T_Townsend_32weeksPREG',
        'T_Townsend_F11',
        'T_Townsend_8mtns',
        'T_Townsend_F11',
        'rbmi_Mom',
        'impedance_F7',
        'impedance_F9',
        'impedance_F11'
      )
    )]
    
  } else{
    # Select variables for maternal analyses.
    allEnv = allEnv[grep('Mom', allEnv)]
    df2 = df[, c('IID', allEnv)]
  
    # Rename to a clean name
    colnames(df2)[2] = var
    
    # Now merge directly (no reshaping needed)
    mydata_long = merge(mydata_long, df2, by = "IID", all.x = TRUE)
    
    return(mydata_long)
  }
  
  # Extract the IID and all environmental column
  df2 = df[, c('IID', allEnv)]
  
  
  # Standardise environmental variable names across visits.
  # Environmental variables may have been measured at different visits. The following conditions rename the available measurements to the corresponding outcome visit and, where necessary, carry measurements forward to subsequent visits.
  if (length(allEnv) > 1) {
    # Special case: frequency of sweet fruit juice consumption.
    # F9 is used for the age-7 outcome and F11 is used for age 15, 18 and 24 outcomes.
    if (var == 'FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice') {
      
      df2 = df2 %>% dplyr::rename(
        "FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice.7" = "FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice_F9",
        "FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice.15" = "FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice_F11"
      )
      df2$FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice.18 = df2$FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice.15
      df2$FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice.24 = df2$FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice.15
      
      
     # Variables measured at F7 and F13. # F7 is used for the age-7 outcome and F13 is used for age 15,
    # 18 and 24 outcomes.
    } else if (length(allEnv) == 2 & sum(grepl('F7|F13', allEnv)) == 2) { 
      
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F7")] = paste0(var, ".7")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F13")] = paste0(var, ".15")
      df2[, paste0(var, ".18")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".15")]
      df2[, paste0(var, ".24")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".15")]
     
    # Variables measured at F7 and F9.
    # F7 is used for the age-7 outcome and F9 is used for age 15, 18 and 24 outcomes. 
    } else if (length(allEnv) == 2 & sum(grepl('F7|F9', allEnv)) == 2) { # Measured at F7 and F9
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F7")] = paste0(var, ".7")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F9")] = paste0(var, ".15")
      df2[, paste0(var, ".18")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".15")]
      df2[, paste0(var, ".24")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".15")]
    
    # Variables measured at F11 and F15.
    # The F11 measurement is assigned to the baseline outcome visit and F15 is used for the later outcome visits.
    } else if (length(allEnv) == 2 & sum(grepl('F11|F15', allEnv)) == 2) { 

      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F11")] = paste0(var, ".0")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F15")] = paste0(var, ".15")
      df2[, paste0(var, ".18")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".15")]
      df2[, paste0(var, ".24")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".15")]
    
    # Variables measured at the same four outcome visits.  
    } else if (length(allEnv) == 4 & sum(grepl('F7|F15|F18|F24', allEnv)) == 4) { # Only the same visit, will just change the _F for .
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F7")] = paste0(var, ".7")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F15")] = paste0(var, ".15")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F18")] = paste0(var, ".18")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F24")] = paste0(var, ".24")
    
    # Special case: household income quintile.
    } else if (var == 'T_Income_Quintile') { # Special one
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_2000")] = paste0(var, ".7")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_2004")] = paste0(var, ".15")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_2007")] = paste0(var, ".18")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_2010")] = paste0(var, ".24")
    
    # Variables measured at F13, F15 and F18.
    # F13 is assigned to the age-7 outcome, F15 to age 15 and F18 is carried forward to the age-24 outcome.
    } else if (length(allEnv) == 3 & sum(grepl('F13|F15|F18', allEnv)) == 3) { 
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F13")] = paste0(var, ".0")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F15")] = paste0(var, ".15")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F18")] = paste0(var, ".18")
      df2[, paste0(var, ".24")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".18")]
    
    # Variables measured at F7, F15 and F18.
    # F7 is used for the age-7 outcome, F15 for age 15 and F18 is carried forward to the age-24 outcome.
    } else if (length(allEnv) == 3 & sum(grepl('F7|F15|F18', allEnv)) == 3) { # Visit at F7, F15, F18
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F7")] = paste0(var, ".7")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F15")] = paste0(var, ".15")
      colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F18")] = paste0(var, ".18")
      df2[, paste0(var, ".24")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".18")]
    } 
    
  } else if (var != 'ProcessedDietScore') { # If only one environmental factor, will copy for each visit
    colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == allEnv] = paste0(var, ".7")
    df2[, paste0(var, ".15")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".7")]
    df2[, paste0(var, ".18")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".7")]
    df2[, paste0(var, ".24")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".7")]
  }
  
 # Special case: processed diet score.
 if (var == 'ProcessedDietScore') {
    colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == paste0(var, "_F13")] = paste0(var, ".13")
    df2[, paste0(var, ".15")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".13")]
    df2[, paste0(var, ".18")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".13")]
    df2[, paste0(var, ".24")] = df2[, paste0(var, ".13")]
  }
    
  # Check if any column contains ".0 or .13"
  if(any(grepl("\\.0$|\\.13$", colnames(df2)))){
    df2 <- df2[, !grepl("(\\.0$|\\.13$|\\.7$|_.*7$)", colnames(df2))]
  }
    
  df2 <- df2 %>% rename_with(~ sub("_F", ".", .x))
  phenotype_cols <- grep(paste0("^", phenotype, "\\."), colnames(df2), value = TRUE)
  new_names <- sub(paste0("^", phenotype), "Phenotype", phenotype_cols)
  df2 <- df2 %>% rename_at(vars(all_of(phenotype_cols)), ~ new_names)

  mydata_long2 = reshape(
    df2,
    idvar = "IID",
    sep = ".",
    varying = colnames(df2)[grep('.', colnames(df2), fixed = TRUE)],
    direction = "long"
  )
 
  # Remove the time column, since it will be duplicated during the merge
  mydata_long2 = mydata_long2[, !(colnames(mydata_long2) %in% c('time'))]
  
  # The rownames is the same : ID.Visit, so we merge by this
  mydata_long = merge(mydata_long, mydata_long2, by = 0, sort = FALSE)
  rownames(mydata_long) = mydata_long[, 1] # The merge will remove the rownames and put it in the first column. I don't want that for the next merge! So keep it as rownames and remove the new column
  mydata_long = mydata_long[, -1]
  
  # Since the IID column is present in both, I will remove the duplicated and rename (IID.x to IID)
  mydata_long = mydata_long[, !(colnames(mydata_long) %in% c('IID.y'))]
  colnames(mydata_long)[1] = 'IID'
  
  return(mydata_long)

}
```

# Main Script 
## Data preprocessing 

```{r}
df=readRDS('processed_pheno.rds')

# Keep only the child
df$IID <- df$IID_child
df=df[grep('A',df$IID),]

# Binary outcomes 
t2dVariable=c('dysglycemie','InsulinResistance') 

# My exposure name 
columnBMI = 'prepreg_bmi'

# Creating phenotype (outcome) and exposure dataframe
all_pheno_bmi = data.frame(
  Factor = rep(columnBMI, 2),
  Phenotype = c('dysglycemie', 'InsulinResistance')
)

# Creating data frame with phenotype (outcome) and child covariates of interest  
Env_Child <- data.frame(
   Factor = c('FreqDrinkSweetFruitJuice','HealthAwareScore', 'ProcessedDietScore', 'MPVAmvpa', 'MPVAsedentary', 'impedance', 'T_Income_Quintile', 'T_Townsend'),
  Phenotype = c(rep('dysglycemie', 8), rep('InsulinResistance', 8))
  )

# Creating data frame with phenotype (outcome) and mother covariates of interest  
Env_Mom <- data.frame(
   Factor = c('ConfectionaryDietScore_32weeksPREG_Mom','ProcessedDietScore_32weeksPREG_Mom','VegetarianDietScore_32weeksPREG_Mom','PhysicalActivity_PREG_Mom', 'TobaccoSmokedREG_EndPREG_Mom', 'TobaccoSmokedREG_1to3mtnsPREG_Mom', 'TobaccoSmokedREG_PrePREG_Mom'),
  Phenotype = c(rep('dysglycemie', 7), rep('InsulinResistance', 7))
  )


```

## GEE: Base covariates 

This section runs the complete GEE analysis for each exposure–outcome pair and separately for the combined-sex, male, and female analyses. It includes only base covariates (sex of the child and the mother's age at delivery)

```{r}

for (whichSex in 0:2) {#0 = mixte, 1=male, 2=female
  nameSex = c('Mixte', 'Male', 'Female')
  
  whichResultName = paste0('/GEE_results/GEE.Base.', nameSex[whichSex + 1], '.rds') # Name for the results outcome file
  
  allResult = NULL
 
  for (j in 1:nrow(all_pheno_bmi)) { # For each pair of VAR-outcome from the table defined above
    
    var = all_pheno_bmi[j, 1] # Extract VAR
    phenotype = all_pheno_bmi[j, 2] # Extract outcome

    # Result 
    allResult_S = t(as.data.frame(c(var, phenotype)))
    colnames(allResult_S) = c('VAR', 'Phenotype')
    allResult_S = as.data.frame(allResult_S)
    
   
    df2 = df[, c(
      'IID',
      var, 
      paste0('age_yrs_', c('F7', 'F15', 'F18', 'F24')),
      paste0(phenotype, '_', c('F7', 'F15', 'F18', 'F24')),
      'sex',
      'AgeDelivery_Mom'
    )]
    
    
    # Rename repeated-measures variables to a common format for reshaping
    df2 = df2 %>% dplyr::rename(
      "age_yrs.7" = "age_yrs_F7",
      "age_yrs.15" = "age_yrs_F15",
      "age_yrs.18" = "age_yrs_F18",
      "age_yrs.24" = "age_yrs_F24",
      "Phenotype.7" = paste0(phenotype, "_F7"),
      "Phenotype.15" = paste0(phenotype, "_F15"),
      "Phenotype.18" = paste0(phenotype, "_F18"),
      "Phenotype.24" = paste0(phenotype, "_F24")
    )
    
    # Rename the exposure to VAR for consistency across models
    colnames(df2)[colnames(df2) == var] = 'VAR' # Will be easier for regression
    
    # Reshape the repeated-measures data from wide to long format
    mydata_long = reshape(
      df2,
      idvar = "IID", # Shared variable across visit
      sep = ".", # Separator
      varying = colnames(df2)[grep('.', colnames(df2), fixed = TRUE)], # Which variable is not constant across visit
      direction = "long"
    )
    # Remove observations with missing outcome values
    mydata_long = mydata_long[!is.na(mydata_long$Phenotype), ] # Remove NA
    
    # Create the quadratic time term for candidate models
    mydata_long$timesq <- mydata_long$time^2
    
    mydata_long = prepareGEEData(mydata_long, 'Phenotype')
    
    if (whichSex != 0) { # If sex-stratified, only keep one sex and remove column sex
      mydata_long = mydata_long[mydata_long$sex == whichSex, ]
      mydata_long = mydata_long[, !(colnames(mydata_long) %in% 'sex')]
    }

    id = length(unique(colsplit(rownames(na.omit(mydata_long)) , '\\.', c('A', 'B'))$A)) # Count the number of unique individual
    allResult_S$N_id = paste0(nrow(na.omit(mydata_long)), ' (', id, ')') # Count the number of observation
    
    
    
    #################################################################
    check1_MeanAcrossTime(mydata_long, phenotype)
    
    #################################################################
    out = check2_BestLinearModel(mydata_long, allResult_S)
  
    allResult_S = out$allResult_S
    best_model_linear = allResult_S$best_linear_model
    smod1 = out$smod1
    smod2 = out$smod2
    smod3 = out$smod3
    smod4 = out$smod4
    
    mod1 = out$mod1
    mod2 = out$mod2
    mod3 = out$mod3
    mod4 = out$mod4
  
    # Define the GEE model formulas according to the best-fitting time structure identified above.
    if(best_model_linear=='mod1'){
      formula='Phenotype ~ VAR + time + AgeDelivery_Mom'
      formula2='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + AgeDelivery_Mom'
    }else if(best_model_linear=='mod2'){
      formula='Phenotype ~ VAR + time + timesq + AgeDelivery_Mom'
      formula2='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + timesq + AgeDelivery_Mom'
      mydata_long$timesq=mydata_long$time*mydata_long$time
    }else if(best_model_linear=='mod3'){
      formula='Phenotype ~ VAR + time + timesq + AgeDelivery_Mom'
      formula2='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + timesq + AgeDelivery_Mom'
      mydata_long$timesq=mydata_long$time*mydata_long$time
    }else if(best_model_linear=='mod4'){
      formula='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + timesq + AgeDelivery_Mom'
      formula2='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + VAR * timesq + AgeDelivery_Mom'
      mydata_long$timesq=mydata_long$time*mydata_long$time
    }
    
    if (whichSex == 0) {
      formula=paste0(formula,' + sex')
      formula2=paste0(formula2,' + sex')
    }
  
    #################################################################
    # Fit the GEE models and extract results 
    allResult = extract_results(
      allResult,
      allResult_S,
      mydata_long,
      formula,
      formula2,
      best_model_linear
    )
    allResult = unique(allResult)
    
    
  }
  
  saveRDS(allResult, whichResultName)
  dev.off()
}
```

## GEE: Env variables - child 

This section runs the complete GEE analysis for each child covariate–outcome pair and separately for the combined-sex, male, and female analyses.
```{r}
nameSex = c('Mixte', 'Male', 'Female')
for(whichSex in 0:2){#0 = mixte, 1=male, 2=female
  # Name of the result file

  whichResultName = paste0('/GEE_results/GEE.env.child.', nameSex[whichSex + 1], '.rds') # Name for the results outcome file
  
  allResult = NULL
  
  for (j in 1:nrow(Env_Child)) { 
    var = Env_Child[j, 1] # Extract factor
    phenotype = Env_Child[j, 2] # Extract outcome
  
    allResult_S = t(as.data.frame(c(var, phenotype)))
    colnames(allResult_S) = c('VAR', 'Phenotype')
    allResult_S = as.data.frame(allResult_S)

    if (var == 'sex' && whichSex != 0) { 
      next
    }
    
    # Create outcome dataset
    df2 = df[, c(
      'IID',
      paste0('age_yrs_', c('F7', 'F15', 'F18', 'F24')),
      paste0(phenotype, '_', c('F7', 'F15', 'F18', 'F24')),
      'sex'
    )]
    
    # Rename outcome and age variables
    df2 <- df2 %>%
      rename_with(~ sub("_F", ".", .x))
    
    phenotype_cols <- grep(
      paste0("^", phenotype, "\\."),
      colnames(df2),
      value = TRUE
    )
    
    new_names <- sub(
      paste0("^", phenotype),
      "Phenotype",
      phenotype_cols
    )
    
    df2 <- df2 %>%  rename_at(vars(all_of(phenotype_cols)), ~ new_names)
    
    # Reshape outcome data
    mydata_long = reshape(
      df2,
      idvar = "IID",
      sep = ".",
      varying = colnames(df2)[grep(".", colnames(df2), fixed = TRUE)],
      direction = "long"
    )
    
    # Remove missing outcomes
    mydata_long = mydata_long[!is.na(mydata_long$Phenotype), ]
    
    # Add environmental variable
    mydata_long = getColumn(mydata_long, var, "Child")
      
      
    mydata_long = prepareGEEData(mydata_long, 'Phenotype')
    
    # Change the name of the factor for VAR, easier later
    colnames(mydata_long)[grep(var, colnames(mydata_long))] = 'VAR'
    mydata_long = mydata_long[!is.na(mydata_long$VAR), ]
    
    mydata_long$timesq <- mydata_long$time^2 # For a specific model
    
    
    if (whichSex != 0) { # Sex-stratified analysis
      mydata_long = mydata_long[mydata_long$sex == whichSex, ]
      mydata_long = mydata_long[, !(colnames(mydata_long) %in% 'sex')]
    }
    
    id = length(unique(colsplit(rownames(na.omit(mydata_long)) , '\\.', c('A', 'B'))$A)) # Count the number of unique individual
    allResult_S$N_id = paste0(nrow(na.omit(mydata_long)), ' (', id, ')') # Count the number of observation
    
    
    
    #################################################################
    # Check 1
    check1_MeanAcrossTime(mydata_long, phenotype)

    
    #################################################################
    # Check 2
    out = check2_BestLinearModel(mydata_long, allResult_S, var, adjust_maternal_age = FALSE)
    allResult_S = out$allResult_S

    # Store the fitted models used to assess model fit and predictions.
    best_model_linear = allResult_S$best_linear_model
    smod1 = out$smod1
    smod2 = out$smod2
    smod3 = out$smod3
    smod4 = out$smod4
    
    mod1 = out$mod1
    mod2 = out$mod2
    mod3 = out$mod3
    mod4 = out$mod4
    
  
    # Define the GEE model formulas according to the best-fitting time structure identified above.
    if(best_model_linear=='mod1'){
      formula='Phenotype ~ VAR + time'
      formula2='Phenotype ~ VAR * time'
    }else if(best_model_linear=='mod2'){
      formula='Phenotype ~ VAR + time + timesq'
      formula2='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + timesq'
      mydata_long$timesq=mydata_long$time*mydata_long$time
    }else if(best_model_linear=='mod3'){
      formula='Phenotype ~ VAR + time + timesq'
      formula2='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + timesq'
      mydata_long$timesq=mydata_long$time*mydata_long$time
    }else if(best_model_linear=='mod4'){
      formula='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + timesq'
      formula2='Phenotype ~ VAR * time + VAR * timesq'
      mydata_long$timesq=mydata_long$time*mydata_long$time
    }
    
    if (whichSex == 0 && var!='sex') {
      formula=paste0(formula,' + sex')
      formula2=paste0(formula2,' + sex')
    }
    
    

    
    #################################################################
    allResult = extract_results(
      allResult,
      allResult_S,
      mydata_long,
      formula,
      formula2,
      best_model_linear
    )
    allResult = unique(allResult)
    
  }
  
  saveRDS(allResult, whichResultName)
  dev.off()
}
```

## GEE: Base + Env

This will test all mom and child environmental variables that were significant (from previous analysis) and combine them together 

```{r}

for(whichSex in 0:2){
  
  ## For the naming be automatic
  nameSex = c('Mixte', 'Male', 'Female')
  
  allResult_Final = c()
  
  withBMIcie = TRUE # Do we want BMI, impedance and fat percent in the multivariable?
  
  if (withBMIcie) {
    addOn = '.WithBMIcie'
  } else{
    addOn = ''
  }
  
  ## Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold
  seuilP = 0.05 / 9
  
  
  # Load results from the previous GEE analyses
  ### Results from the VAR
  whichResultName = paste0('/GEE_results/GEE.Base.', nameSex[whichSex + 1], '.rds')
  resultVAR = readRDS(whichResultName)
  
  ### Results from the Environmental - child
  whichResultName = paste0('/GEE_results/GEE.env.child.', nameSex[whichSex + 1], '.rds')
  resultEnv = readRDS(whichResultName)
  resultEnv$Age = 'Child'
  
  ### Results from the Environmental - Mom
  whichResultName = paste0('/GEE_results/GEE.env.mother.', nameSex[whichSex + 1], '.rds')
  resultEnvMom = readRDS(whichResultName)
  resultEnvMom$Age = 'Mom'
  
  resultEnv = rbind(resultEnv, resultEnvMom)
  
  
  ## Generate the environmental df for each outcome
  for (d in t2dVariable) {
    
    # Extract results for current outcome
    resultVAR_t = resultVAR[resultVAR$Phenotype == d, ]
    resultEnv_t = resultEnv[resultEnv$Phenotype == d, ]
    
    
    # Select environmental variables that were significant in the # previous analyses.
    resultEnv_t = resultEnv_t[(resultEnv_t$best_linear_model %in% c('mod1','mod2') & resultEnv_t$VAR_cont_p < seuilP) | (resultEnv_t$best_linear_model %in% c('mod3','mod4') & resultEnv_t$VAR_int_p < seuilP) |  (resultEnv_t$best_linear_model %in% c('mod3','mod4') & resultEnv_t$VARtime_int_p < seuilP), ]
    

    
    # Keep only the information needed to construct the ## multivariable model.
    resultEnv_t_filt = resultEnv_t[, c('VAR', 'Age', 'best_linear_model')]
    
    if (withBMIcie) {
      resultEnv_t_filt = resultEnv_t_filt[resultEnv_t_filt$VAR != 'sex', ] 
    } else{
      resultEnv_t_filt = resultEnv_t_filt[!grepl('Fat|bmi|imped', resultEnv_t_filt$VAR) & resultEnv_t_filt$VAR != 'sex', ] 
    }
    
    ## Keep the selected base covariates and their best-fitting models
    resultVAR_t_filt = resultVAR_t[, c('VAR', 'best_linear_model')]
    
    # Extract column for only basic variable/covariables
    df2 = df[, c('IID',
                 paste0('age_yrs_', c('F7', 'F15', 'F18', 'F24')),
                 paste0(d, '_', c('F7', 'F15', 'F18', 'F24')),
                 'AgeDelivery_Mom',
                 'sex' )]
    
    # Rename the covaraite/outcome
    df2 = df2 %>% dplyr::rename(
      "age_yrs.7" = "age_yrs_F7",
      "age_yrs.15" = "age_yrs_F15",
      "age_yrs.18" = "age_yrs_F18",
      "age_yrs.24" = "age_yrs_F24",
      "Phenotype.7" = paste0(d, "_F7"),
      "Phenotype.15" = paste0(d, "_F15"),
      "Phenotype.18" = paste0(d, "_F18"),
      "Phenotype.24" = paste0(d, "_F24")
    )
    
    # Reshape 
    mydata_long = reshape(
      df2,
      idvar = "IID",
      sep = ".",
      varying = colnames(df2)[grep('.', colnames(df2), fixed = TRUE)],
      direction = "long"
    )
    ## Remove observations with a missing outcome
    mydata_long = mydata_long[!is.na(mydata_long$Phenotype), ] 

    mydata_long = prepareGEEData(mydata_long, 'Phenotype')
    mydata_long$timesq <- mydata_long$time^2 # Create the quadratic time term
    
    mydata_long$IID = dplyr::min_rank(mydata_long$IID)
    mydata_long = mydata_long[order(mydata_long$IID), ]
    
    
    # # Add the significant environmental variables to the longitudinal dataset and standardise them.
    if (nrow(resultEnv_t_filt) != 0) { 
      for (f_p in 1:nrow(resultEnv_t_filt)) {
        mydata_long = getColumn(mydata_long, resultEnv_t_filt[f_p, 'VAR'], resultEnv_t_filt[f_p, 'Age'])
        mydata_long=scaleTheVariableAndRemoveOutlier(mydata_long,resultEnv_t_filt[f_p, 'VAR'])
      }

      colNames = colnames(mydata_long)
      
      # Check for collinearity among the environmental variables. 
      colNames = colNames[!(
        colNames %in% c(
          'IID',
          'Phenotype',
          'AgeDelivery_Mom',
          'age_yrs',
          'sex',
          'time',
          'timesq'
        )
      )]
      colNames_F = paste(colNames, collapse = ' + ') # Generate the formula containing all environmental factors
      colNames_F = paste0('Phenotype ~ ', colNames_F) # Add the outcome to the formula
      
      m <- geeglm(
        as.formula(colNames_F),
        data = mydata_long,
        id = IID,
        family = binomial,
        corstr = "exchangeable"
      )
      
      
      ## Remove environmental variables with VIF >= 5
      vif_result = check_collinearity(m)
      vif_result5 = vif_result[vif_result$VIF >= 5, "Term"]
      colNames = colNames[!(colNames %in% vif_result5)]
    } 
    
    # Prepare for GEE with VAR + Env
    ## Generate the environmental formula
    formu = c('Phenotype ~ time + AgeDelivery_Mom')
    if (whichSex == 0) {
      formu = paste0(formu, ' + sex')
    }
    
    # Add each selected environmental variable to the model according # to its best-fitting longitudinal model.
    if (nrow(resultEnv_t_filt) != 0) {
      for (cN in colNames) {
        best_model = resultEnv_t_filt[resultEnv_t_filt$VAR == cN, 'best_linear_model'] # Get which best model for the factor
        if (best_model == 'mod1') {
          formu = paste0(formu, ' + ', cN) # If it is mod1, only add the factor to the formula
        } else if (best_model == 'mod4') {
          formu = paste0(formu, ' + ', cN, '*time +', cN, '*timesq') # If the complex is the best, add interaction with time and time2
        }else if (best_model == 'mod2') {
          formu = paste0(formu, ' + ', cN) 
          if(!grepl('timesq',formu)){
            formu = paste0(formu, ' + timesq')
          }
        }else if(best_model=='mod3'){
          formu = paste0(formu, ' + ', cN,'*time') 
          if(!grepl('timesq',formu)){
            formu = paste0(formu, ' + timesq')
          }
        }
      }
    }
    
    if(whichSex!=0){ # If sex-stratified
      mydata_long=mydata_long[mydata_long$sex==whichSex,]
      mydata_long=mydata_long[,!(colnames(mydata_long)=='sex')]
    }

    
    # Fit a separate multivariable GEE model for each selected base covariate/VAR.
    for (nVAR in resultVAR_t_filt$VAR) { # For each VAR
      best_model_VAR = resultVAR_t_filt[resultVAR_t_filt$VAR == nVAR, 'best_linear_model']
      
      ## Start with the environmental/base-covariate model and add ## the current VAR according to it       best-fitting model.
      formu_temp = formu 
      if (best_model_VAR == 'mod1') {
        formu_temp = gsub('~', '~ VAR +', formu_temp)
      } else if (best_model_VAR == 'mod4') {
        formu_temp = gsub('~', '~ VAR*time + VAR*timesq +', formu_temp)
      } else if (best_model_VAR == 'mod2') {
        formu_temp = paste0(formu_temp, ' + VAR')
        if (!grepl('timesq', formu_temp)) {
          formu_temp = paste0(formu_temp, ' + timesq')
        }
      } else if (best_model_VAR == 'mod3') {
        formu_temp = paste0(formu_temp, ' + VAR*time')
        if (!grepl('timesq', formu_temp)) {
          formu_temp = paste0(formu_temp, ' + timesq')
        }
      }
      
      # Add the current base covariate to the data.
      mydata_long_temp = mydata_long
      mydata_long_temp$IID=colsplit(rownames(mydata_long_temp),'\\.',c('A','B'))$A # Recover the individual ID
      df_VAR = df[, c('IID', nVAR)] # Add the VAR to the table
      colnames(df_VAR)[2] = 'VAR'
      mydata_long_temp = merge(mydata_long_temp, df_VAR, by = 'IID') # Merge
      mydata_long_temp = na.omit(mydata_long_temp) # retain complete cases
      
      ## Re-index individuals and order the observations
      mydata_long_temp$IID = dplyr::min_rank(mydata_long_temp$IID)
      mydata_long_temp = mydata_long_temp[order(mydata_long_temp$IID), ] 
      
      # Fit the final multivariable GEE model.
      best_total <- geeglm(
        as.formula(formu_temp),
        data = mydata_long_temp,
        id = IID,
        family = binomial,
        corstr = "exchangeable"
      )
      
      
      # Aummarize an lme object (gets beta hat, se, t-value, p-value for fixed effects)
      outputm1 <- (texreg::extract(best_total))
      tabl = data.frame(
        Name = attr(outputm1, 'coef.names'),
        Value = attr(outputm1, 'coef'),
        Std.Error = attr(outputm1, 'se'),
        p.value = attr(outputm1, 'pvalues')
      )
      rownames(tabl) = tabl$Name
      
      # Extract result depending on the best models, again, only mod1 and mod4 in my case
      b = round(tabl['VAR', 'Value'], digits = 6)
      se = round(tabl['VAR', 'Std.Error'], digits = 6)
      p = formatC(tabl['VAR', 'p.value'], format = "e", digits = 2)
      
      ## For models without a time interaction, interaction estimates are not applicable.
      if (best_model_VAR %in% c('mod1','mod2')) {
        b_t = NA
        se_t = NA
        p_t = NA
        
        b_t2 = NA
        se_t2 = NA
        p_t2 = NA
      } else if (best_model_VAR == 'mod4') {
        ## Extract the linear time interaction.
        if (sum(rownames(tabl) == 'time:VAR') == 1) {
          b_t = round(tabl['time:VAR', 'Value'], digits = 6)
          se_t = round(tabl['time:VAR', 'Std.Error'], digits = 6)
          p_t = formatC(tabl['time:VAR', 'p.value'], format = "e", digits = 6)
        } else{
          b_t = round(tabl['VAR:time', 'Value'], digits = 6)
          se_t = round(tabl['VAR:time', 'Std.Error'], digits = 6)
          p_t = formatC(tabl['VAR:time', 'p.value'], format = "e", digits = 6)
        }
        
        ## Extract the quadratic time interaction.
        if (sum(rownames(tabl) == 'timesq:VAR') == 1) {
          b_t2 = round(tabl['timesq:VAR', 'Value'], digits = 6)
          se_t2 = round(tabl['timesq:VAR', 'Std.Error'], digits = 6)
          p_t2 = formatC(tabl['timesq:VAR', 'p.value'], format = "e", digits = 6)
        } else{
          b_t2 = round(tabl['VAR:timesq', 'Value'], digits = 2)
          se_t2 = round(tabl['VAR:timesq', 'Std.Error'], digits = 2)
          p_t2 = formatC(tabl['VAR:timesq', 'p.value'], format = "e", digits = 6)
        }
      }
      
      # Record the number of observations and unique individuals.
      n_id = length(unique(mydata_long_temp$IID))
      n_tot = nrow(mydata_long_temp)
      n = paste0(n_tot, ' (', n_id, ')')
      
      # Store the results for the current outcome, sex, and VAR.
      line = t(as.data.frame(
        c(
          d,
          nameSex[whichSex + 1],
          nVAR,
          formu_temp,
          n,
          b,
          se,
          p,
          b_t,
          se_t,
          p_t,
          b_t2,
          se_t2,
          p_t2
        )
      ))
      rownames(line) = NULL
      colnames(line) = c(
        'Phenotype',
        'Sex',
        'VAR',
        'Formula',
        'NTot_NID',
        'b_VAR',
        'se_VAR',
        'p_VAR',
        'b_VARtime',
        'se_VARtime',
        'p_VARtime',
        'b_timesq',
        'se_timesq',
        'p_timesq'
      )
      allResult_Final = rbind(allResult_Final, line)
    }
    
    
  }
  
  saveRDS(allResult_Final,
          paste0('/GEE_results/GEE.Full.', nameSex[whichSex + 1], addOn, '.rds'))
}
  
```
